function: Trains SIM amplitudes and phases as an electromagnetic neural network that encodes an image and steers a beam to the receive antenna of its class (p. 1, 3).
system: Single-antenna transmitter with a transmissive stacked intelligent metasurface (SIM, N=441 meta-atoms per layer); receiver ULA with one antenna per class (M=2 to 10); 28 GHz; Rician link (p. 2, 4).
method: Supervised training of the SIM coefficients as an electromagnetic neural network, using Adam mini-batch gradient descent and a cross-entropy loss on MNIST (p. 3-4).
data_channel: MNIST digits (public); own simulated Rician block-fading channel, K=3 dB, path loss with exponent 2.8, at 28 GHz; no 3GPP model or measurements (p. 3-4).
test_conditions: MNIST train/test split 6:1, noise added in training; test accuracy for each setting of L, N, distance, and class count, each with its own training curve (p. 4-5).
baselines: none; only parameter sweeps of the proposed SIM-based EMNN (layers, meta-atoms, distance, classes) (p. 4-5).
metrics: Recognition accuracy versus epoch on the MNIST test set, confusion matrix for ten digits, and received energy distribution across the receiving array (p. 5).
q1_support: p. 3: "we adopt the Rician fading model". Custom simulator with a textbook fading model and a power-law path loss (p. 4); no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, or measured channel is used.
q2_support: p. 4: "Fig. 2(c) illustrates the recognition accuracy versus the training epoch". Each setting of L, N, distance, and class count is its own training curve; no model trained in one condition is tested in another.
q3_support: p. 4: "we evaluate the effect of the number L of layers on the recognition accuracy". Only sweeps of the proposed SIM; no classical or learned method is compared anywhere in the 6 pages.
q4_support: p. 4: "choosing proper SIM parameters for achieving the desired performance with minimum hardware cost". Qualitative only; no complexity order, operations, parameter count, or runtime is reported.
q5_support: p. 4: "we use the MNIST dataset to evaluate the performance of the proposed SIM-based EMNN". MNIST is the dataset of the learning task, not a channel dataset; the channel is simulated and no code or data link is given.
notes: Borderline on function: the learned parameters are the SIM (a stacked RIS) phases and amplitudes that steer beams (area 3; p. 3: "steer the wireless signals"), but the objective is image-recognition accuracy in task-oriented semantic communication, so the reviewer may judge it outside the seven functions (exclude: function). If included, all five criteria are unmet. The PDF is the arXiv:2407.15053v2 preprint (p. 1) and prints no DOI; its title and letter format agree with the DOI.
